correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real full-rank three-column least-squares matrices with nonadjacent orthogonality and u,v>0, u²+v²<1, normalized complement normals reduce every two-coordinate update to an orthogonal rank-one residual projector. Their Gram inverse K=DGD supplies the normalized sign-witness lower bound 1/(s^TKs). Explicit positive weights p_i=s_i(Ks)_i/(s^TKs) attain the bound because the difference is a sum of two rank-one positive-semidefinite edge matrices. Their common nullspace and linear independence prove uniqueness. Column scaling/sign changes and inconsistent right-hand sides do not alter the error update. Source code at verify.py reproduced exact rational eigenvalues and 43,801 randomized/grid/projector checks. Continuous parameter and infinite-iterate statements depend on proof, not tests.

value.rationale: The theorem completely solves a natural smallest nontrivial batch-selection design (three columns, pair size two) over two freely varying adjacent Gram correlations and arbitrary column scalings. It supplies a unique nonuniform sampling distribution with explicit sharp error factor and proof certificate, rather than merely a sufficient heuristic or generic solver formulation. For u=v=3/5 it gives (4/9,1/9,4/9) and factor 7/9, strictly improving the exact uniform design factor (41+3 sqrt(137))/96. The use is an exact benchmark for fixed batch-probability learning; no unsupported empirical speedup is claimed.
